question:
During an inverse-tangent investigation, two positive acute angles are defined by $A=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$ and $B=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{7}\right)$. The students use the tangent addition and subtraction formulas to combine the angles. Because both $A$ and $B$ lie in $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $B>A$, the signs and principal-value intervals of $A+B$ and $A-B$ can be established before applying $\tan^{-1}$. This prevents an incorrect addition of $\pi$ to the final inverse-tangent expressions.

(a) Calculate $\tan(A+B)$.

(b) Express $A+B$ as a single inverse-tangent principal value.

(c) Calculate $\tan(A-B)$.

(d) Express $A-B$ as a single inverse-tangent principal value and justify its sign.
explanation:
(a)
Using the tangent-addition formula,
$$\tan(A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}$$
$$=\frac{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{7}}{1-\frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{2}{7}}$$
$$=\frac{\frac{15}{28}}{\frac{13}{14}}=\frac{15}{26}$$

(b)
Both $A$ and $B$ are positive. Also, $1-\tan A\tan B=\dfrac{13}{14}>0$, so $A+B<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Therefore, $A+B$ belongs to the principal range of inverse tangent and
$$A+B=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{26}\right)$$

(c)
Using the tangent-difference formula,
$$\tan(A-B)=\frac{\tan A-\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}$$
$$=\frac{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{2}{7}}{1+\frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{2}{7}}$$
$$=\frac{-\frac{1}{28}}{\frac{15}{14}}=-\frac{1}{30}$$

(d)
Since $\dfrac{2}{7}>\dfrac{1}{4}$ and inverse tangent is increasing, $B>A$. Hence, $A-B<0$. The difference lies in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$, so
$$A-B=\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{30}\right)=-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{30}\right)$$
